**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), preferred-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations checked:** § 10.3 (p0063 – the only assignment provision), § 4.1 Term/Termination (p0024), § 4.2 Termination Payment (p0026–p0028), and full-document searches for "assign", "change of control", "successor", "consent", "terminate". No change-of-control or re-pricing trigger exists anywhere.
- **Why it fails fallback:** § 10.3 is purely a binding-effect/"successors and assigns" sentence. It contains none of the fallback elements (successor assignment with written notice, consent for other assignments, reasonableness standard) and, read literally, leaves HDI free to assign — including to a competitor — without our consent. It is not walk-away, since there is no prohibition on our assignment and no vendor change-of-control right.
- **Cure:** a single short clause inserted after § 10.3 carrying all six preferred elements; § 10.3 itself and all surrounding provisions are preserved verbatim, and no non-element boilerplate (notice mechanics, survival, notwithstanding overrides) was added.
